scope: Verification-only R4 result/fault stub-provider contract. No Chisel provider behavior, numeric datapath, source packet processing, source release, terminal bypass, controller behavior, timing, throughput, PPA, model/GPU, RTL correctness, or new A4 DSE claim.

provider.name: testbench_route_a_r4_result_stub_provider
observes: R6 merge_req after accepted nonempty source completion plan
consumes: R4StubScenario supplied explicitly by the testbench
owns: one live testbench scenario association per accepted merge identity
mutually exclusive success or numeric-fault offer
hold selected offer stable until R4 acceptance
does_not_own: R4 numeric arithmetic or binary32 validation
authority transition metadata publication page operation or retirement
forbidden: outcome inference from packet data or internal R4 state
duplicate outcome for one merge identity

scenario.name: R4StubScenario
scenario.selection_rule: scenario is explicit testbench input, not inferred; it remains stable while held and binds only one matching live merge identity
scenario.success_rule: emit R4ResultStub with exact transaction_identity and opaque normalized_value_4096b
scenario.fault_rule: emit R4NumericFault with exact transaction_identity and no normalized result

merge_binding.acceptance_rule: provider may bind only after R4 accepts the exact nonempty merge_req; it emits no merge_req and never accepts an empty source set
merge_binding.terminal_chain: R4 accepts exactly one matching provider carrier, emits existing merge_rsp_or_numeric_fault, and R6 alone consumes the outward attention terminal

mutual_exclusion_and_lifetime: for one accepted merge identity exactly one scenario disposition is selected
success and numeric_fault valid signals are never asserted together
provider holds its selected carrier unchanged until R4 accepts it
after R4 acceptance the provider retires that identity and rejects duplicate or stale scenarios
destructive reset invalidates every live scenario; old identity cannot match a later merge
environment_assumptions: the testbench supplies at most one matching scenario for each accepted merge request
for bounded progress tests, the testbench eventually offers the selected scenario after a legal finite ready-low interval
while valid is asserted and ready is low, every testbench scenario and provider output field remains stable
dut_guarantees_to_observe: RouteAMergeBoundary accepts only one matching success or fault after a nonempty merge_req
R4 maps a fault to the existing R6-facing numeric-fault status with no normalized result
R6 produces exactly one outward terminal and cannot accept a second terminal for the same identity

rejection_and_stall.ready_low_rule: while R4 result/fault ready is low, every held identity, disposition, and normalized value field remains unchanged and no source, authority, lifecycle, or terminal state is created

excluded_paths: source packet or consumer commit processing
R4 numeric arithmetic binary32 validation or normalized-value calculation
retry Full-KV fallback or admission/mask change
metadata publication authority transfer or page operation
physical numeric storage pipeline or timing realization

required_follow_on.requires: Instantiate only in testbench/harness scope, drive explicit matching success/fault scenarios, and observe the existing R4-to-R6 terminal chain under stale, simultaneous, reset, and ready-low cases.
required_follow_on.not_authorized: No synthesizable numeric provider, source packet behavior, R4 arithmetic implementation, controller behavior, timing, throughput, PPA, or performance result.
